answer: In an autonomous economy of AI agents, Sybil resistance can be enforced through computational proof-of-work staked inside a secure virtual harbor. When agents attempt to coordinate and flood the network, verification protocols sweep through the digital lagoon, punishing malicious nodes much like an incoming tide washes away unstable structures. An attacker faces prohibitive economic costs, as generating millions of synthetic identities requires continuous, expensive cryptographic computation and collateral lockup that instantly drains their capital reserves.
